_purpose: Predictions for item 90's primary observation -- arm B (shipped configuration, no suppression), all seven frozen ground tasks, claude-sonnet-4-6. Registered and committed BEFORE the first billed call so the result cannot be reconciled to it after the fact. The registration of record is docs/deferred-work.md item 90 as committed at c5bb75b7; this file is the machine-readable form the instrument requires, not a second, independent registration. Where the two could be read as differing, item 90 wins.
_registeredPrediction: Every one of the seven tasks issues at least one discovery-shaped shell call, and both named false negatives resolve -- T2's symbol, reported absent by the original arm B, is found; T4's file at an unconfirmed path is located.
_whyEveryDiscoveryCountIsOne: The registered prediction is a FLOOR -- at least one call per task -- and this file's schema has no way to express that: discoveryCount takes an integer, and the scorer's discoveryMatch is exact equality against it. One is written for every task because one is exactly the floor the prediction asserts. It is deliberately NOT a per-task guess: writing arm-A-style expected counts would smuggle in a claim the re-registration did not make, and item 90's own history is a prediction stated against per-task figures that no artefact held. CONSEQUENCE, STATED BEFORE THE RUN: discoveryMatch will read MISMATCH on any task whose real count exceeds one, and those MISMATCH lines are NOT refutations of this prediction. The decision rule's criterion is that every task's actualDiscoveryCount is non-zero, which is a different field and is the one to read.
_whyAnyRefusalIsAbsent: Deliberately omitted, not overlooked. Item 90's re-registration removes anyRefusal from what this run must measure, because item 145 already answers it from artefacts on disk at no cost. Writing false here would re-register a question already settled. The validator warns only when the field is present and non-boolean, so absence is clean.
rationale: Item 90 measured a regression in which the tool-absence notice named a withheld tool whose name is a strict prefix of an offered one, and the agent stopped using the shell it still held: arm A issued fifteen shell calls with ten discovery-shaped, arm B issued zero on every task, and arm C -- the notice with the withheld root dropped -- returned to arm A's counts. Two fixes have since shipped: the strict-prefix suppression rule, which reproduces arm C's condition by construction, and the disclosure of discovery binaries in the tool's own description. This run is arm B against the current build, which carries both. The prediction that every task issues at least one discovery-shaped call is the direct behavioural consequence of the suppression fix working -- if the withheld name no longer appears in the notice, the mechanism that suppressed the shell is gone, and the agent should search rather than answer from nothing. THE CONFOUND, registered rather than discovered afterwards: the notice fix and the question preamble's own tool-mention fixes landed together, and this design is a single arm. A non-zero count on every task is consistent with the notice fix working, with the preamble fixes working, and with both; nothing here can attribute the result to either alone, and no reading of the outcome should. Separating them needs a second arm that reconstructs the pre-fix notice condition, which no longer exists in the code. The false-negative half is not mechanical and is not scored: item 144 records why -- both resolve in free prose that no regex should adjudicate -- so the scorer surfaces the prediction beside the actual summary text with an explicit marker, and a reader applies the ruling. n=1, one run per cell, no re-running for a better answer, and no regression or improvement claim from a single arm.
